patch.summary:
Thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — OpenPhone and Zenzap share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.

Comparison thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs. Choose OpenPhone only if your buying job matches “Modern SMB shared business phone (also branded Quo) with shared numbers, SMS and Sona AI —” rather than Zenzap's shape. Choose Zenzap only if your buying job matches “Professional work-chat app for frontline and multi-site teams replacing WhatsApp groups — ” rather than OpenPhone's shape. Workflow advantage: OpenPhone leans business-phone, sales-calling; Zenzap leans shared coverage. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — OpenPhone and Zenzap share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.
- Positioning: OpenPhone is Modern SMB shared business phone (also branded Quo) with shared numbers, SMS and Sona AI — Starter from $15/user/month annual.; Zenzap is Professional work-chat app for frontline and multi-site teams replacing WhatsApp groups — free tier, Pro $3/user/month yearly, Business+ $8 .
- Company-size focus: OpenPhone (solo, small-business, mid-market) vs Zenzap (micro, small-business, mid-market).
- Workflow coverage skew: OpenPhone-leaning business-phone, sales-calling vs Zenzap-leaning —.
- Researched limits: OpenPhone — US/Canada-centric calling footprint — not a global UCaaS carrier story; Zenzap — Integrations with other business tools and API access require Business+.

Limitations — OpenPhone: US/Canada-centric calling footprint — not a global UCaaS carrier story; Phone menus, automatic recording and deeper CRM require Business or above; Zenzap: Integrations with other business tools and API access require Business+; Voice and video calls require Pro; call recording and transcription require Business+.

Poor-fit cases: OpenPhone is a poor fit when that limitation bites: US/Canada-centric calling footprint — not a global UCaaS carrier story · Zenzap is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Integrations with other business tools and API access require Business+ · Avoid OpenPhone if you actually need Zenzap's motion (Professional work-chat app for frontline and multi-site teams replacing WhatsApp)

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
